By definition 𝔫ΠQ,nBPS,+≅H∗⁡ℐ​𝒞​(𝐀2)≅𝐐⁡[2]\mathfrak{n}^{\mathtt{\aBPS},+}_{\Pi_{Q},n}\cong\HO^{*}\mathcal{IC}(\mathbf{A}^{2})\cong\mathbf{Q}[2], and 𝔫ΠQBPS,+\mathfrak{n}^{\mathtt{\aBPS},+}_{\Pi_{Q}} is the cohomologically graded generalised Kac–Moody Lie algebra determined by the weight function

P:ΦΠQ+≅𝐙⩾1→\displaystyle P\colon\Phi^{+}_{\Pi_{Q}}\cong\mathbf{Z}_{\geqslant 1}\rightarrow 𝐍⁡[t±1]\displaystyle\mathbf{N}[t^{\pm 1}]
n↦\displaystyle n\mapsto t−1.\displaystyle t^{-1}.

Precisely, 𝔤ΠQBPS\mathfrak{g}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\aBPS} is the generalised Kac–Moody Lie algebra spanned by elements en,fn,hne_{n},f_{n},h_{n} of respective cohomological degrees −2,2,0-2,2,0 and 𝐙Q0\mathbf{Z}^{Q_{0}}-degree n,0,−nn,0,-n respectively, i.e. the infinite-dimensional Heisenberg algebra. Since all but one of the summands on the right hand side of (10.2) vanish, Theorem 10.5 yields

⨁n⩾0H∗⁡(Hilbn⁡(𝐀2),𝐐vir)≅L1\bigoplus_{n\geqslant 0}\HO^{*}\!(\Hilb_{n}(\mathbf{A}^{2}),\mathbf{Q}^{\mathrm{vir}})\cong L_{1}

where L1=𝐐⁡[e1,e2,…]L_{1}=\mathbf{Q}[e_{1},e_{2},\ldots] is the irreducible lowest weight module for 𝔤ΠQBPS\mathfrak{g}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\mathtt{\aBPS}} of weight 11.

10.4.2. Irreducible lowest weight 𝔤ΠQBPS,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩\mathfrak{g}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\mathtt{\aBPS},\mathcal{SSN}}-modules from Nakajima quiver varieties

In this section we recover Nakajima’s original construction [Nak98] of lowest weight representations of Kac–Moody Lie algebras by restricting to the zeroth cohomological degree in our main theorem (Theorem 10.5) on the representation theory of 𝔤ΠQBPS,△\mathfrak{g}^{\mathtt{\aBPS},\triangle}_{\Pi_{Q}} for the choice △=𝒮​𝒮​𝒩\triangle=\mathcal{SSN}.

Let QQ be a quiver. Let 𝐟∈𝐍Q0\mathbf{f}\in\mathbf{N}^{Q_{0}} be a dimension vector. Consider the CoHA H0⁡(𝒜ΠQ𝒮​𝒮​𝒩,ψ)\HO^{0}(\mathscr{A}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\mathcal{SSN},\psi}) obtained by taking the zeroth cohomologically graded piece of the CoHA H∗⁡𝒜ΠQ𝒮​𝒮​𝒩,ψ\HO^{*}\!\mathscr{A}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\mathcal{SSN},\psi}. Recall that by Theorem 7.9 this is isomorphic to the enveloping algebra of half of the Borcherds–Bozec algebra 𝔤Q\mathfrak{g}_{Q}. By Theorem 1.2, if 𝐝∈ΣΠQ𝐟\mathbf{d}\in\Sigma_{\Pi_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}}} there is an identification between

H0(ι𝒮​𝒮​𝒩!ℐ𝒞(ℳΠQ𝐟,𝐝))\HO^{0}(\iota_{\mathcal{SSN}}^{!}\mathcal{IC}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}},\mathbf{d}}))

and a basis of Chevalley generators of weight 𝐝\mathbf{d} inside 𝔤Q𝐟\mathfrak{g}_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}}: in particular, the above cohomology group vanishes if 𝐝\mathbf{d} is supported at more than one vertex. Applying H0⁡(−)\HO^{0}(-) to the isomorphism

𝕄𝐟𝒮​𝒮​𝒩(Q)≅⨁(𝐝,1)∈ΦQ𝐟+H∗(ι𝒮​𝒮​𝒩!ℐ𝒞(ℳΠQ𝐟,(𝐝,1)))⊗L((𝐝,1),(−,0))Q𝐟\mathbb{M}^{\mathcal{SSN}}_{\mathbf{f}}(Q)\cong\bigoplus_{(\mathbf{d},1)\in\Phi_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}}^{+}}\HO^{*}\!(\iota_{\mathcal{SSN}}^{!}\mathcal{IC}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}},(\mathbf{d},1)}))\otimes L_{((\mathbf{d},1),(-,0))_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}}}

we thus find that every summand apart from the one for (𝐝,1)=(0,…,0,1)∈ΦΠQ𝐟+(\mathbf{d},1)=(0,\ldots,0,1)\in\Phi^{+}_{\Pi_{Q_{\mathbf{f}}}} vanishes, so that we obtain the following theorem

Theorem 10.7.

There is an isomorphism of 𝐔⁡(𝔤Q)=H0⁡(𝒜ΠQ𝒮​𝒮​𝒩,ψ)\UEA(\mathfrak{g}_{Q})=\HO^{0}(\mathscr{A}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\mathcal{SSN},\psi})-modules

⨁𝐝∈𝐍Q0H0(N𝒮​𝒮​𝒩(Q,𝐝,𝐟),ι𝒮​𝒮​𝒩!𝐐vir)≅L−𝐟⋅.\bigoplus_{\mathbf{d}\in\mathbf{N}^{Q_{0}}}\HO^{0}(N^{\mathcal{SSN}}(Q,\mathbf{d},\mathbf{f}),\iota_{\mathcal{SSN}}^{!}\mathbf{Q}^{\mathrm{vir}})\cong L_{-\mathbf{f}\cdot}.

Here, we denote by L−𝐟⋅L_{-\mathbf{f}\cdot} the simple lowest weight module of 𝔤Q\mathfrak{g}_{Q} of lowest weight 𝐝↦−𝐟⋅𝐝\mathbf{d}\mapsto-\mathbf{f}\cdot\mathbf{d}, the usual dot product as in §2. In the special case in which QQ has no loops, this is Nakajima’s original theorem [Nak98, Thm.10.2]. In the case in which there are loops, this is a CoHA analogue of results in [Boz16] on highest weight crystals for the Borcherds–Bozec algebra.

11. Equivariant parameters

11.1. Deformed BPS algebra

In this section, we explain how to adapt the main results of this paper when we turn on equivariant parameters. We let 𝒜\mathcal{A} and 𝙹𝙷:𝔐𝒜→ℳ𝒜\JH\colon\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}} be as in §4. We let GG be an algebraic group and we assume that GG acts on 𝙹𝙷\JH and that this action is compatible with the direct sum morphism: if GG acts diagonally on 𝔐𝒜×𝔐𝒜\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\times\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}, the direct sum morphism ⊕:𝔐𝒜×𝔐𝒜→𝔐𝒜\oplus\colon\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\times\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\rightarrow\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}} is GG-equivariant. To avoid discussing group actions on stacks [Rom05], we assume that each connected component of 𝔐𝒜\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}} is a global quotient stack X/HX/H of an algebraic variety XX by an algebraic group HH, and GG acts on XX giving a G×HG\times H-action on XX (i.e. the GG and HH actions commute with each other).

We indicate by the GG-superscript the objects and maps induced when taking the stack-theoretic quotient by GG. For example, we let 𝔐𝒜G≔𝔐𝒜/G\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\coloneqq\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}/G (for a given connected component X/HX/H of 𝔐𝒜\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}, there is a connected component X/(H×G)X/(H\times G) of 𝔐𝒜G\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}), ℳ𝒜G≔ℳ𝒜/G\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\coloneqq\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}/G, 𝙹𝙷G:𝔐𝒜G→ℳ𝒜G\JH^{G}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}, ⊕G:ℳ𝒜G×B​Gℳ𝒜G→ℳ𝒜G\oplus^{G}\colon\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}. Note that the source of the map ⊕G\oplus^{G} can be identified with the stack quotient (ℳ𝒜×ℳ𝒜)/G(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\times\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}})/G by the diagonal action of GG.

We have the (smooth) quotient map π:ℳ𝒜→ℳ𝒜G\pi\colon\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}, and the commutative square

(11.1)

is Cartesian.

The categories Perv⁡(ℳ𝒜G)​[dimG]\operatorname{Perv}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G], MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G)​[dimG]\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G], 𝒟c+​(ℳ𝒜G)\mathcal{D}^{+}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}) and 𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G))\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})) all carry a symmetric monoidal tensor product defined by ℱ⊡G𝒢≔⊕∗G(ℱ⊠𝒢)\mathscr{F}\boxdot^{G}\mathscr{G}\coloneqq\oplus_{*}^{G}(\mathscr{F}\boxtimes\mathscr{G}).

By smooth base change in the diagram (11.1), π∗:𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G))→𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜))\pi^{*}\colon\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}))\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}})) is a symmetric monoidal functor, mapping objects of MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G)​[dimG]\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G] to objects of MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜)\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}). We have a similar statement for the constructible derived categories and the categories of perverse sheaves.

We define 𝐐¯𝔐𝒜Gvir\underline{\mathbf{Q}}_{\mathfrak{M}^{G}_{\mathcal{A}}}^{\mathrm{vir}} by setting its restriction to the connected component 𝔐𝒜,aG\mathfrak{M}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},a}, to be 𝐐¯𝔐𝒜,aG⊗𝐋(a,a)𝒞/2\underline{\mathbf{Q}}_{\mathfrak{M}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},a}}\otimes\mathbf{L}^{(a,a)_{\mathscr{C}}/2}, as in the non-equivariant case §6.1. We gather in the following proposition the properties of the GG-equivariant versions of the main objects of this paper. Parts (1) and (3) follow from (4), and the analogous results for G={1}G=\{1\}.

Proposition 11.1.
  1. (1)

    The mixed Hodge module complex 𝒜¯𝒜G≔(𝙹𝙷𝒜G)∗​𝐐¯𝔐𝒜Gvir\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}\coloneqq(\JH_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})_{*}\underline{\mathbf{Q}}_{\mathfrak{M}^{G}_{\mathcal{A}}}^{\mathrm{vir}} is pure of weight zero, concentrated in cohomological degrees ⩾−dimG\geqslant-\dim G.

  2. (2)

    The relative CoHA has the structure of an algebra object in 𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G))\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})) defined as in [DHS22] (working over B​G\mathrm{B}G). We denote by 𝔪G\mathfrak{m}^{G} the multiplication map.

  3. (3)

    The degree −dimG-\dim G cohomology ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,AlgG≔ℋ−dimG(𝒜¯𝒜G)[dimG]\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{G}\coloneqq\mathcal{H}^{-\dim G}(\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G] has an induced algebra structure. It is an algebra object in MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G)​[dimG]\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G].

  4. (4)

    We have canonical identifications of algebra objects π∗​𝒜¯𝒜G=𝒜¯𝒜\pi^{*}\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}=\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}, π∗​ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,AlgG=ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,Alg\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}=\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}.

11.2. Deformed relative BPS Lie algebra

For l∈𝐍l\in\mathbf{N} and m′∈K⁡(𝒜)m^{\prime}\in\K(\mathcal{A}), we let

umG:ℳ𝒜,m′G→ℳ𝒜,l​m′Gu_{m}^{G}\colon\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},lm^{\prime}}^{G}

be the map obtained by composing the diagonal morphism ℳ𝒜,m′G→ℳ𝒜,m′G×B​G…×B​Gℳ𝒜,m′G\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G}\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\ldots\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G} with the (iterated) direct sum morphism ℳ𝒜,m′G×B​G…×B​Gℳ𝒜,m′G→ℳ𝒜,l​m′G\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G}\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\ldots\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},lm^{\prime}}^{G}. We let

𝒢¯𝒜,mG≔{ℐ​𝒞¯​(ℳ𝒜,mG)​[dimG] if m∈ΣK⁡(𝒜)(umG)∗​ℐ​𝒞¯​(ℳ𝒜,m′G)​[dimG] if m=l​m′∈Φ+iso with m′∈ΣK⁡(𝒜) and l⩾20 otherwise.\underline{\mathscr{G}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},m}\coloneqq\left\{\begin{aligned} &\underline{\mathcal{IC}}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m}^{G})[\dim G]\quad&\text{ if $m\in\Sigma_{\K(\mathcal{A})}$}\\ &(u_{m}^{G})_{*}\underline{\mathcal{IC}}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A},m^{\prime}}^{G})[\dim G]\quad&\text{ if $m=lm^{\prime}\in\Phi^{\mathrm{iso}}_{+}$ with $m^{\prime}\in\Sigma_{\K(\mathcal{A})}$ and $l\geqslant 2$}\\ &0\quad&\text{ otherwise.}\end{aligned}\right.

The construction of GKM Lie algebras and their enveloping algebras in the symmetric monoidal category of mixed Hodge modules on a monoid in the category of schemes as in §3.5 adapts in a straightforward way to the situation where ℳ\mathcal{M} is replaced by a stack quotient of ℳ\mathcal{M} by an algebraic group GG and one works relatively over B​G\mathrm{B}G. We let ℳG≔ℳ/G\mathcal{M}^{G}\coloneqq\mathcal{M}/G and the direct sum map is a (finite) morphism ⊕:ℳG×B​GℳG→ℳG\oplus\colon\mathcal{M}^{G}\times_{\mathrm{B}G}\mathcal{M}^{G}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}^{G}. The free algebra is defined accordingly and one can make sense of Serre relations in the same way as for schemes, and we have the following:

Theorem 11.2.

We have a canonical isomorphism of algebra objects in MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G)\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})

𝐔⁡(𝔫K⁡(𝒜),(−,−)𝒞,𝒢¯𝒜G+)≅ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,AlgG.\UEA(\mathfrak{n}^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A}),(-,-)_{\mathscr{C}},\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}})\cong\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}.
Proof.

The forgetful functor π∗:MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G)​[dimG]→MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜)\pi^{*}\colon\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G})[\dim G]\rightarrow\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}) is monoidal and conservative. Therefore, Theorem 11.2 follows from Theorem 1.1. ∎

We can therefore define (as in the case G={1}G=\{1\}) the relative BPS Lie algebra as

ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,LieG≔𝔫K⁡(𝒜),(−,−)𝒞,𝒢¯𝒜G+.\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Lie}}^{G}\coloneqq\mathfrak{n}^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A}),(-,-)_{\mathscr{C}},\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}}.

As in §8.3.2, we define a PBW map

(11.2) Ψ𝒜ψ,G:Sym⊡G(ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,LieG⊗H𝐂∗∗)→𝒜¯𝒜G.\Psi_{\mathcal{A}}^{\psi,G}\colon\Sym_{\boxdot^{G}}\left(\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Lie}}^{G}\otimes\HO^{*}_{\mathbf{C}^{*}}\right)\rightarrow\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}.
Theorem 11.3 (PBW isomorphism).

The map Ψ𝒜ψ,G\Psi_{\mathcal{A}}^{\psi,G} is an isomorphism of mixed Hodge module complexes.

Proof.

The forgetful functor π∗:𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G))→𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜))\pi^{*}\colon\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}))\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}})) is conservative. Therefore, Theorem 11.3 follows from Theorem 1.7. ∎

11.3. Deformed absolute BPS Lie algebra

One of the key facts used to deduce results for the absolute CoHA from results for the relative CoHA (for example the GKM description and PBW isomorphism) is the compatibility of the derived global sections functor

𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜))→𝒟+​(MHM⁡(K⁡(𝒜)))\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}))\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\K(\mathcal{A})))

with the respective monoidal tensor products. In the equivariant setting, this compatibility no longer holds in general. The derived global section functor

𝒟+​(MHM⁡(ℳ𝒜G))→𝒟+​(MHM⁡(K⁡(𝒜)/G))\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}))\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{+}(\mathrm{MHM}(\K(\mathcal{A})/G))

(where GG acts trivially on K⁡(𝒜)\K(\mathcal{A}) and K⁡(𝒜)/G\K(\mathcal{A})/G is a quotient stack) is not monoidal for the tensor structures induced by the direct sum (as in §11.1), that is for a given complex variety XX and GG-equivariant mixed Hodge modules ℱ¯,𝒢¯\underline{\mathscr{F}},\underline{\mathscr{G}} on XX, the natural map

(11.3) H∗(X/G,ℱ¯)⊗H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)H∗(X/G,𝒢¯)→H∗(X/G×B​GX/G,ℱ¯⊠𝒢¯)\HO^{*}(X/G,\underline{\mathscr{F}})\otimes_{\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q})}\HO^{*}(X/G,\underline{\mathscr{G}})\rightarrow\HO^{*}(X/G\times_{\mathrm{B}G}X/G,\underline{\mathscr{F}}\boxtimes\underline{\mathscr{G}})

may not be an isomorphism. Nevertheless, it is an isomorphism under certain hypotheses on ℱ¯,𝒢¯\underline{\mathscr{F}},\underline{\mathscr{G}} and GG.

Lemma 11.4.

Let XX be an algebraic variety acted on by an algebraic group GG. We assume that H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}) is pure. We let r:X/G→B​Gr\colon X/G\rightarrow\mathrm{B}G be the natural map and π:X→X/G\pi\colon X\rightarrow X/G be the quotient map. We let ℱ¯,𝒢¯\underline{\mathscr{F}},\underline{\mathscr{G}} be mixed Hodge modules on X/GX/G such that r∗​ℱ¯r_{*}\underline{\mathscr{F}} and r∗​𝒢¯r_{*}\underline{\mathscr{G}} are pure mixed Hodge modules on B​G\mathrm{B}G. Then, the Künneth map (11.3) is an isomorphism. More precisely, we have

H∗⁡(X/G,ℱ¯)=H∗⁡(X,π∗​ℱ¯)⊗H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(X/G,\underline{\mathscr{F}})=\HO^{*}(X,\pi^{*}\underline{\mathscr{F}})\otimes\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q})

and similarly for 𝒢¯\underline{\mathscr{G}}.

Proof.

The Leray–Serre spectral sequence for the fibration rr computing H∗⁡(X/G,ℱ¯)\HO^{*}(X/G,\underline{\mathscr{F}}) degenerates at the second page Ep,q2=Hp⁡(B⁡G,ℋq​(r∗​ℱ¯))=Hp+dim(G)⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)⊗Hq−dim(G)⁡(X,π∗​ℱ¯)E^{2}_{p,q}=\HO^{p}(\B G,\mathcal{H}^{q}(r_{*}\underline{\mathscr{F}}))=\HO^{p+\dim(G)}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})\otimes\HO^{q-\dim(G)}(X,\pi^{*}\underline{\mathscr{F}}) for purity reasons. ∎

This proof shows more generally that the Künneth map is an isomorphism when both H∗⁡(X/G,ℱ)\HO^{*}(X/G,\mathscr{F}) and H∗⁡(X/G,𝒢)\HO^{*}(X/G,\mathscr{G}) are free over H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q}). In the sequel, we assume that the mixed Hodge modules 𝒢¯𝒜,mG\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A},m}^{G}, m∈ΦK⁡(𝒜)+m\in\Phi^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A})} defined in §11.2 are such that the Künneth map is an isomorphism for any pair 𝒢¯𝒜,mG,𝒢¯𝒜,nG\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A},m}^{G},\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A},n}^{G}. We say that the mixed Hodge modules 𝒢¯𝒜,mG\underline{\mathscr{G}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},m}, m∈ΦK⁡(𝒜)+m\in\Phi^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A})} satisfy the Künneth property. Then it follows formally that there is an isomorphism of Lie algebras

(11.4) H∗⁡(𝔫ℳ𝒜G,(−,−)𝒞,𝒢¯𝒜G+)≅𝔫K⁡(𝒜),(−,−)𝒞,𝒢¯𝒜+⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐).\HO^{*}(\mathfrak{n}^{+}_{\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G},(-,-)_{\mathscr{C}},\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G}})\cong\mathfrak{n}^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A}),(-,-)_{\mathscr{C}},\underline{\mathscr{G}}_{\mathcal{A}}}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}).

We immediately deduce the following.

Theorem 11.5.

Assume that the mixed Hodge modules 𝒢¯𝒜,mG\underline{\mathscr{G}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},m}, m∈ΦK⁡(𝒜)+m\in\Phi^{+}_{\K(\mathcal{A})} satisfy the Künneth property. The deformed BPS algebra BPS𝒜,AlgG\mathrm{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{G} is isomorphic to the enveloping algebra of the generalised Kac–Moody algebra defined over H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q}), associated to the monoid with bilinear form (K⁡(𝒜),(−,−)𝒞)(\K(\mathcal{A}),(-,-)_{\mathscr{C}}) and the weight function described in Theorem 1.2 (with ι△\iota_{\triangle} the identity morphism here – nilpotent versions are considered in Proposition 11.12). In particular, there is an isomorphism of algebras

BPS𝒜,AlgG≅BPS𝒜,Alg⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐).\mathrm{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{G}\cong\mathrm{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}).
Proof.

The fact that the mixed Hodge modules 𝒢¯𝒜,mG\underline{\mathscr{G}}^{G}_{\mathcal{A},m} satisfy the Künneth property implies that the H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})-algebra obtained by taking derived global sections of ℬ​𝒫​𝒮𝒜,AlgG\mathcal{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{G} is exactly the H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})-linear enveloping algebra of the GKM as described in the statement of the theorem. Theorem 11.5 is then a consequence of Theorem 11.2. ∎

Given a choice of positive determinant bundle on 𝔐𝒜G\mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{G} we define a map

(11.5) SymH∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)⁡(BPS¯𝒜,LieG⊗H𝐂∗∗)→H∗⁡(𝒜¯𝒜ψ,G)\Sym_{\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})}\left(\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Lie}}^{G}\otimes\HO^{*}_{\mathbf{C}^{*}}\right)\rightarrow\HO^{*}(\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\psi,G})

as in §8.3.2 by using the algebra structure on H∗⁡(𝒜¯𝒜ψ,G)\HO^{*}(\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\psi,G}), the H𝐂∗∗\HO^{*}_{\mathbf{C}^{*}}-action on the CoHA and the iterated CoHA multiplication.

Theorem 11.6 (Deformed PBW theorem).

The map (11.5) is an isomorphism of mixed Hodge module complexes.

Proof.

The Künneth property implies that the map (11.5) coincides with the map H∗⁡(Ψ𝒜ψ,G)\HO^{*}(\Psi_{\mathcal{A}}^{\psi,G}). Therefore, Theorem 11.6 follows from Theorem 11.3. ∎

11.4. Examples

When 𝒜\mathcal{A} is the category of representations of the preprojective algebra ΠQ\Pi_{Q} of a quiver, there is a natural choice for the group GG. Namely, we let

Gar≔∏i∈Q0Sp2​gi×∏i≠j∈Q0GLqi,j,G_{\mathrm{ar}}\coloneqq\prod_{i\in Q_{0}}\mathrm{Sp}_{2g_{i}}\times\prod_{i\neq j\in Q_{0}}\mathrm{GL}_{q_{i,j}},

be the group of arrow symmetries of Q¯\overline{Q} preserving the moment map, where gig_{i} is the number of loops at the vertex ii in Q1Q_{1} and qi,jq_{i,j} the number of arrows between ii and jj in Q¯\overline{Q} [MO19, §2.1.3]. The group GarG_{\mathrm{ar}} acts naturally on the representation spaces 𝐀Q¯,𝐝\mathbf{A}_{\overline{Q},\mathbf{d}} defined in §2. Indeed, we can write

𝐀Q¯,𝐝=∏i∈Q0End⁡(𝐂di)⊗𝐂2​gi×∏i≠j∈Q0T∗​(Hom⁡(𝐂di,𝐂dj)⊗𝐂qi,j),\mathbf{A}_{\overline{Q},\mathbf{d}}=\prod_{i\in Q_{0}}\operatorname{End}(\mathbf{C}^{d_{i}})\otimes\mathbf{C}^{2g_{i}}\times\prod_{i\neq j\in Q_{0}}\mathrm{T}^{*}(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{C}^{d_{i}},\mathbf{C}^{d_{j}})\otimes\mathbf{C}^{q_{i,j}}),

where qi,jq_{i,j} is the number of arrows i→ji\rightarrow j in QQ, Sp2​gi\mathrm{Sp}_{2g_{i}} acts on 𝐂2​gi\mathbf{C}^{2g_{i}} and GLqi,j\mathrm{GL}_{q_{i,j}} acts on 𝐂qi,j\mathbf{C}^{q_{i,j}}.

We can take for GG any (connected) subgroup of Gar×𝐂∗G_{\mathrm{ar}}\times\mathbf{C}^{*}. The additional 𝐂∗\mathbf{C}^{*} action rescales cotangent fibers (i.e. if (x,x∗)∈𝐀Q¯,𝐝(x,x^{*})\in\mathbf{A}_{\overline{Q},\mathbf{d}} and u∈𝐂∗u\in\mathbf{C}^{*}, u⋅(x,x∗)=(x,u​x∗)u\cdot(x,x^{*})=(x,ux^{*}). For example, GG can be a maximal torus of GarG_{\mathrm{ar}}.

As shown in the following lemma, equivariant formality holds for the mixed Hodge modules involved in the description of the BPS algebra of ΠQ\Pi_{Q}.

Lemma 11.7.

Let QQ be a quiver, ΠQ\Pi_{Q} its preprojective algebra and 𝐝∈𝐍Q0\mathbf{d}\in\mathbf{N}^{Q_{0}} a dimension vector. Then, IHn​(ℳΠQ,𝐝)\mathrm{IH}^{n}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}}) vanishes for nn odd. Therefore, for any connected linear algebraic group GG acting on ℳΠQ,𝐝\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}}, the intersection cohomology complex is naturally equivariant and IH^*⁡(ℳΠQ,𝐝/G)=IHG∗​(ℳΠQ,𝐝)≅IH^*⁡(ℳΠQ,𝐝)⊗𝐐H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)\ICA(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}}/G)=\mathrm{IH}^{*}_{G}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}})\cong\ICA(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}})\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q}).

Proof.

The last statement is known as “equivariant formality” and follows from the purity of the intersection cohomology. Purity, as well as vanishing of odd intersection cohomology, follow from Theorem 1.1 by taking derived global sections, and the analogous purity and vanishing statements for HBM⁡(𝔐ΠQ,𝐐vir)\HO^{\BoMo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Pi_{Q}},\mathbf{Q}^{\mathrm{vir}}): this is [Dav23a, Theorem A]. ∎

11.5. 3d deformed BPS Lie algebra

One can define the deformed 3d BPS Lie algebra using the tripled quiver with potential and dimensional reduction. It is defined as in §8.1 after upgrading objects to mixed Hodge modules as in [DM20]. The group Gar×𝐂∗G_{\mathrm{ar}}\times\mathbf{C}^{*} acts on the representation space 𝐀Q~,𝐝≅𝐀Q¯,𝐝×∏i∈Q0End⁡(𝐂di)\mathbf{A}_{\widetilde{Q},\mathbf{d}}\cong\mathbf{A}_{\overline{Q},\mathbf{d}}\times\prod_{i\in Q_{0}}\operatorname{End}(\mathbf{C}^{d_{i}}) of the tripled quiver as follows. The action on the first factor is as defined in §11.4. The subgroup GarG_{\mathrm{ar}} acts trivially on the second factor and the additional copy of 𝐂∗\mathbf{C}^{*} acts by rescaling the factor ∏i∈Q0End⁡(𝐂di)\prod_{i\in Q_{0}}\operatorname{End}(\mathbf{C}^{d_{i}}) by u−1u^{-1}. For this action, the canonical potential W~\widetilde{W} gives a Gar×𝐂∗G_{\mathrm{ar}}\times\mathbf{C}^{*}-invariant function on 𝐀Q~,𝐝\mathbf{A}_{\widetilde{Q},\mathbf{d}}. The vanishing cycle cohomology gives the cohomological Hall algebra 𝒜¯Q~,W~ψ,G\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi,G}, and the perverse filtration together with dimensional reduction provides us with the 3d BPS Lie algebra ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯ΠQ,Lie𝟹​𝚍,ψ,G\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\mathtt{3d},\psi,G}. It is an object of the shifted category of mixed Hodge modules MHM⁡(ℳΠQG)​[dimG]\mathrm{MHM}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{G})[\dim G]. All results presented in §8 hold for the GG-equivariant deformations of the relative and absolute versions of the BPS algebra and Lie algebra:

Proposition 11.8.

We have a canonical isomorphism of Lie algebra objects in mixed Hodge modules

ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯ΠQ,Lie𝟹​𝚍,ψ,G≅ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯ΠQ,LieG.\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\mathtt{3d},\psi,G}\cong\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{G}.
Proof.

Again, by conservativity of the forgetful functor, it suffices to check this statement when GG is the trivial group and in this case, this is Theorem 1.16. ∎

As in the non-equivariant setting, the 3d BPS Lie algebra 𝔤Q~,W~ψ,G\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi,G} is obtained by passing to derived global sections of ℬ​𝒫​𝒮ΠQ,Lie𝟹​𝚍,G\mathcal{BPS}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\mathtt{3d},G}. The following is our main result on deformations of BPS Lie algebras for tripled quivers with potential: it says that all deformations obtained by switching on equivariant parameters associated to arrows of the quiver are trivial.

Corollary 11.9.

There is an isomorphism of Lie algebras

𝔤Q~,W~ψ,G≅𝔤Q~,W~ψ⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐).\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi,G}\cong\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}).
Proof.

We have 𝔤Q~,W~ψ≅𝔫ΠQψ\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi}\cong\mathfrak{n}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\psi} by Theorem 1.16 and 𝔤Q~,Wψ,G≅𝔫ΠQψ,G\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},W}^{\psi,G}\cong\mathfrak{n}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\psi,G} by Proposition 11.8. The isomorphism then follows from (11.4).

∎

11.6. Equivariant cohomology of Nakajima quiver varieties

Our description of the whole cohomology of Nakajima quiver varieties (§10) adapts to the equivariant setting. As in [MO19, §2.1.2], the group Gar×𝐂∗G_{\mathrm{ar}}\times\mathbf{C}^{*} acts on quiver varieties and since they have pure cohomology, equivariant formality holds for them for any action of a connected linear algebraic group G⊆Gar×𝐂∗G\subseteq G_{\mathrm{ar}}\times\mathbf{C}^{*} (as in Lemma 11.7). The description of the GG-equivariant cohomology of quiver varieties as a direct sum of lowest modules (Theorem 10.5) adapts to the GG-equivariant cohomology in a straightforward way: this eventually amounts to extending the scalars from 𝐐\mathbf{Q} to H∗⁡(B​G,𝐐)\HO^{*}(\mathrm{B}G,\mathbf{Q}).

11.7. Nilpotent versions

If ℳ𝒜△⊆ℳ𝒜\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}} is a saturated submonoid stable under the GG-action on ℳ𝒜\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}, then one can define the corresponding relative and absolute CoHAs 𝒜¯𝒜△,ψ,G\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle,\psi,G} and H∗⁡(𝒜¯𝒜△,ψ,G)\HO^{*}(\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle,\psi,G}), and the △\triangle BPS algebra and △\triangle Lie algebra BPS¯𝒜,Alg△,ψ,G\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle,\psi,G} and BPS¯𝒜,Lie△,G\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\triangle,G} via ι△!\iota_{\triangle}^{!}, as before. In particular, this applies to the case of the preprojective algebras of quivers and △∈{𝒩,𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{N},\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\}. The results of §10 also translate to the equivariant BPS algebras with various nilpotency conditions. Crucial in the step from relative to absolute CoHAs is again the equivariant formality of the sheaf cohomologies involved. For the nilpotent versions, this equivariant formality follows again from the odd cohomology vanishing.

Proposition 11.10.

The stacks 𝔐ΠQ△\mathfrak{M}_{\Pi_{Q}}^{\triangle} for △∈{𝒩,𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{N},\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\} are pure and have no odd cohomology. △\triangle Nakajima quiver varieties are pure and have no odd cohomology for △∈{𝒩,𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{N},\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\}.

Proof.

The first statement is [SV20, Theorem A], for △∈{𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\}. For △=𝒩\triangle=\mathcal{N} it holds for the BPS Lie algebra since it is Verdier dual to the BPS Lie algebra 𝔤ΠQ\mathfrak{g}_{\Pi_{Q}}, and then cohomological integrality implies it for the cohomology of the whole stack.

The second statement comes from the fact that all nilpotent versions of Nakajima quiver varieties are very ℓ\ell-pure and polynomial count (when working over a finite field 𝐅q\mathbf{F}_{q} and ℓ\ell-adic cohomology, for ℓ\ell and qq coprime), [Hau10, Theorem 1]. Alternatively, they follow from the first statement and cohomological wall crossing, i.e. [Dav23a, Theorem C]. ∎

Corollary 11.11.

For △∈{𝒩,𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{N},\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\}, the complexes of mixed Hodge modules ι△!ℐ​𝒞¯(ℳΠQ,𝐝)\iota_{\triangle}^{!}\underline{\mathcal{IC}}(\mathcal{M}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathbf{d}}) have pure cohomology, and vanishing odd cohomology.

In summary, we can generalise the results of this section for our chosen three Serre subcategories:

Proposition 11.12.

For △∈{𝒩,𝒮​𝒩,𝒮​𝒮​𝒩}\triangle\in\{\mathcal{N},\mathcal{SN},\mathcal{SSN}\} there are isomorphisms of Lie algebras

𝔤Q~,W~△,ψ,G≅𝔤Q~,W~△,ψ⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)≅𝔫ΠQ△,+⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐),\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\triangle,\psi,G}\cong\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\triangle,\psi}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})\cong\mathfrak{n}^{\triangle,+}_{\Pi_{Q}}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}),

an isomorphism of algebras

BPS¯𝒜,Alg△,ψ,G≅BPS¯𝒜,Alg△,ψ⊗H∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐).\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle,\psi,G}\cong\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle,\psi}\otimes\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q}).

as well as a PBW isomorphism (not respecting the algebra structures on the domain and the target)

SymH∗⁡(B⁡G,𝐐)⁡(BPS¯𝒜,Lie△,G⊗H𝐂∗∗)→H∗⁡(𝒜¯𝒜△,ψ,G).\Sym_{\HO^{*}(\B G,\mathbf{Q})}\left(\underline{\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\triangle,G}\otimes\HO^{*}_{\mathbf{C}^{*}}\right)\rightarrow\HO^{*}(\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle,\psi,G}).

Here, the algebra 𝔤Q~,W~△,ψ,G\mathfrak{g}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\triangle,\psi,G} is defined as the derived global sections of (ı△G)!ℬ𝒫𝒮Q~,W~ψ,G(\imath_{\triangle}^{G})^{!}\mathcal{BPS}_{\widetilde{Q},\widetilde{W}}^{\psi,G} where ı△G:ℳQ~△/G→ℳQ~/G\imath^{G}_{\triangle}\colon\mathcal{M}_{\widetilde{Q}}^{\triangle}/G\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\widetilde{Q}}/G is the inclusion of the saturated submonoid of ℳQ~\mathcal{M}_{\widetilde{Q}} of representations of Q~\widetilde{Q} such that the underlying representation of Q¯\overline{Q} has the property △\triangle.

This is the perverse sheaf ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯ΠQ,Lie𝟹​𝚍\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\mathtt{3d}} on which the Lie algebra structure is induced by the monomorphism ℬ​𝒫​𝒮ΠQ,Lie𝟹​𝚍→ℬ​𝒫​𝒮ΠQ,Algψ\mathcal{BPS}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Lie}}^{\mathtt{3d}}\rightarrow\mathcal{BPS}_{\Pi_{Q},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\psi} (page 8.2).

A.3. Nilpotent versions

Let ı△:ℳ𝒜△→ℳ𝒜\imath_{\triangle}\colon\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{A}} be the inclusion of a saturated locally closed submonoid. For example, 𝒜¯𝒜△=ı△!𝒜¯𝒜\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle}=\imath_{\triangle}^{!}\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}, 𝒜𝒜△=ı△!𝒜𝒜\mathscr{A}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle}=\imath_{\triangle}^{!}\mathscr{A}_{\mathcal{A}}, ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,Alg△=ı△!ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,Alg\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle}=\imath_{\triangle}^{!}\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}, ℬ𝒫𝒮𝒜,Alg△=ı△!ℬ𝒫𝒮𝒜,Alg\mathcal{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle}=\imath_{\triangle}^{!}\mathcal{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}, and we have the ψ\psi-twisted versions of these four algebra objects, 𝒜¯𝒜△,ψ\underline{\mathscr{A}}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle,\psi}, 𝒜𝒜△,ψ\mathscr{A}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\triangle,\psi}, ℬ​𝒫​𝒮¯𝒜,Alg△,ψ\underline{\mathcal{BPS}}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle,\psi} and ℬ​𝒫​𝒮𝒜,Alg△,ψ\mathcal{BPS}_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{Alg}}^{\triangle,\psi} (page 6.1).

A.4. Equivariant versions

We add a superscript GG to indicate the GG-equivariant versions of the objects considered (page 11).

    N⁡(Q,𝐝,𝐟)N(Q,\mathbf{d},\mathbf{f}) the smooth Nakajima quiver variety constructed from the doubled quiver Q¯\overline{Q}, with dimension vector 𝐝\mathbf{d} and framing dimension vector 𝐟\mathbf{f} (page 10.2).
